pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
A very warm welcome to St Edward’s
By considering St Edward’s for your child, you are opening the door to a nurturing, inclusive and vibrant community where young people don’t just learn — they flourish. Our school is alive with opportunity, curiosity and encouragement, enabling every pupil to discover their strengths, grow in confidence and embrace the joy of learning.
Outstanding academic results matter, but they are only part of what our pupils gain during their time with us. Our true purpose is to ignite imagination, inspire ambition and instil the self-belief that empowers young people to shape their own futures. We cultivate inquisitive minds, resilient spirits and a lifelong love of learning — qualities that extend far beyond the classroom.
Children thrive when they feel happy, secure and valued. That is why our commitment to pastoral care is as strong as our dedication to academic excellence. We prioritise wellbeing, belonging and character development, ensuring every pupil feels known, supported and ready to meet challenges with confidence.
At St Edward’s, education is personal. Children are at the heart of every decision we make. We celebrate individuality, recognise potential and shape each child’s journey around who they are and who they can become. Alongside knowledge, we nurture thinkers, problem-solvers, communicators and collaborators — young people prepared not only for exams, but for life.
Mrs Anna Sandford-Squires Headteacher

One Family. One Journey. Only 13 Minutes Away.
From 9 Months to 18 Years.
A warm welcome to families from Rendcomb College. We understand that the closure of Rendcomb College will bring uncertainty for families, pupils and staff as you consider your next steps. At such a time, reassurance, clarity and kindness matter.
St Edward’s School Cheltenham, together with Ashley Manor Preparatory School, forms the St Edward’s Family, offering a joined-up independent education from 9 months to 18 years.
From the early years through to GCSEs and A Levels, our focus is on strong pastoral care, academic ambition and smooth, well-planned transitions, within a calm environment where every child is known, supported and able to thrive.
Both Ashley Manor Preparatory School and St Edward’s School Cheltenham are located just 13 minutes from Rendcomb, making visits and transition straightforward for families in the area. A dedicated minibus service is also available to support pupils and provide additional flexibility.
Why Choose St Edward’s School Cheltenham (11 to 18 years)
Families joining St Edward’s benefit from:
Our size is intentional. Smaller cohorts allow for individual attention, confidence-building and leadership opportunities, helping pupils feel secure, supported and ambitious about their future.
One Family, One Journey (9 Months–18 Years)
Ashley Manor Preparatory School provides Nursery and Prep education from 9 months to 11 years and forms the preparatory stage of the St Edward’s Family.
Set within 45 acres of beautiful parkland, Ashley Manor offers a calm, nurturing start to a child’s education. Outdoor learning is central to our curriculum, supporting confidence, wellbeing and independence, while strong pastoral care ensures every child is known and supported as they grow.
These early foundations prepare children smoothly for the next stage of their journey into St Edward’s School Cheltenham.
👉 Discover Ashley Manor Preparatory School
Stability, Governance & Long-Term Commitment
St Edward’s is proud to be part of Alpha Schools, a well-established group of 19 independent schools across England.
Alpha Schools provides:
Each school within the group retains its own identity, leadership and ethos, while benefiting from the strength and security of the wider organisation. For families seeking confidence and continuity during a period of change, this provides an important foundation of stability.
Long-term financial stability and strong governance.
Personal Tours
We would be very happy to speak with you personally, answer questions and support you as you explore whether St Edward’s or Ashley Manor could be the right next step for your child.
👉 To book for St Edward's
Complete the form below, or call +44 (0)1242 388555, and a member of our Admissions Team will be in touch to arrange your visit and discuss how we can support your child during this transition.
👉 To book for Ashley Manor :
For earlier years or siblings aged 9 months to 11, please call + 44 (0)1242 388550 or visit Discover Ashley Manor. A member of the Admissions will be in touch to arrange your visit and discuss next steps.

Outstanding Education
Proudly co-educational and academically non-selective, we are a small school for big ideas and big dreams. With small class sizes and low student-to-teacher ratio, our focus is truly on each individual, and on providing a bespoke pathway for every child.
We believe that every one of our students is capable of extraordinary things, and our dedicated staff take pride in creating a warm and supportive environment in which every child can explore, discover and refine their gifts and talents, whilst at the same time providing the structure for them to exceed their potential in the classroom.
We are proud of our vibrant community, our excellent teaching, our wealth of facilities and our exceptional pastoral care.
Our academic results speak for themselves; St Edward’s students invariably surpass their baseline assessment grades. The value-added goes far beyond examinations. Our children become confident, capable, passionate learners, with the self-discipline, resilience and strength of identity to tackle every opportunity that life brings.
Our children excel because they are happy, comfortable and thrive on the array of opportunities in drama, music, sport, CCF, trips (in the UK and across the globe), adventures and real-life experiences.
Discover what makes St Edward’s unique. Discover outstanding education.
Since starting at St Edward’s our son has learnt so much. The quality of teaching and the care and attention the teachers give to their pupils has impressed us.

Performing Arts Technician
St Edward’s School is seeking an enthusiastic, skilled and reliable Performing Arts Technician to join our Performing Arts Department from September 2026.
This is an exciting opportunity for a technically confident theatre practitioner to play an important role in supporting our programme of music, drama and performing arts, including examinations, showcases, school productions and external performances.
This hands-on, varied role includes both technical and administrative responsibilities, with occasional evening and weekend work for events and shows.
About St Edward’s School
At St Edward’s we have high expectations of all members of our school community, from our pupils to our staff. Excellent teaching and pastoral care in our nurturing and encouraging environment allow our pupils and staff to flourish.
Our small class sizes mean that our teachers really know pupils as individuals and can provide tailored support to maximise achievement. Our school motto means to strive for the best and that is exactly what we want for everyone in our school.
Contract Type: Part time, flexible (1-2 days per week)
Salary: £14-18 per hour (based on experience)
Start Date: September 2026
Why Work at St Edward’s School?
To find out more about our role, please read our Job Description.
If you are passionate about empowering young people, we encourage you to apply!
To apply for this role, please fill out our Application Form and return this to [email protected] along with your CV.
We look forward to welcoming you to St Edward’s School.
St Edward’s School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children. Applicants for ALL jobs will undergo appropriate child-protection screening including checks with past employers and the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check to enhanced level, with costs covered by the company. This role is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 and the Amendments to the Exceptions Order 1975, 2013 and 2020.

Music
Music is a very exciting part of the School, and we are fortunate in having a large number of dedicated peripatetic teachers offering lessons in most musical instruments and musical theory.
Timetables are arranged throughout the day on a rotating system so that music students do not miss the same subject on a regular basis.
Students who are interested in Music are asked to join one of the Choirs, Orchestra, Concert Band and other Music Ensembles. It is expected that all instrumental students will be involved in at least one co-curricular activity as is appropriate to the individual.
Major performances held during the year include the Carol Service in Tewkesbury Abbey and the Pump Room Concert in the Spring Term. We have also previously performed in the Scratch Youth Messiah at the Royal Albert Hall.
At many events, students have an opportunity to perform solo pieces (both instrumental and vocal) as well as orchestral and choral works. One of these opportunities is participating in the annual concert held in Cheltenham’s Pittville Pump Room at the end of the Spring Term. Informal concerts are held after school at regular intervals throughout the year.
Drama
In addition to regular curriculum Drama lessons, the School stages one main whole school production a year.
Click here to read our outstanding review of Legally Blonde by the National School Theatre Awards.
Productions & Clubs
We aim to provide a varied programme of school productions. Auditions are open to all students regardless of experience and usually take place early in September. Dates and times are advertised in Drama lessons, assemblies and through Form Tutors. Senior School productions take place in the Spring Term. Performances are usually on Thursday, Friday and Saturday evenings. If the project is appropriate, sometimes we offer separate Lower School and Upper School productions.
The St Edward’s Stage Crew takes responsibility for the technical and backstage work in the School. This includes school plays, assemblies and many other events. Our Stage Crew take considerable but supervised responsibility during these major events and are as widely involved as possible backstage. The Stage Crew do not meet on a regular basis but come together for specific projects.
There are a range of drama activities on offer as part of our co-curricular programme of clubs and activities.
Private Lessons are available in Speech and Drama. Lessons take place before School in the morning, during lunchtime or after 4pm. Students have the opportunity to pursue the Grade Examinations of The London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art (LAMDA). These examinations are in Verse and Prose and/or Acting. There are also opportunities to participate in the Cheltenham Festival of Performing Arts.
Communicating and presenting in public are valuable skills for further education and adult life. Learning these at school gives students an advantage when entering university, as well as providing achievement and fun during their schooldays. UCAS points are awarded for success in Grades 6, 7 and 8.

Clubs & Societies
Co-curricular clubs and societies are a great way to ignite interest and engage our students in new hobbies, as well as extend the work completed in lessons. By nurturing existing interests and encouraging new and exciting passions our students are able to flourish into the rounded, community-minded young adults that St Edward’s students are.​​​​​
A comprehensive list of the co-curricular activities on offer is provided to students and parents each term. In addition to our wide range of clubs and societies. Supervised study is also available every day after school from 4.15pm to 6.00pm.
Co-Curricular Categories
Our co-curricular programme is designed around six categories of activity:
Physical activities help students to develop fundamental movement skills and physical literacy. There are opportunities to learn and master both core and advanced skills in a variety of activities and sports. Activities also help to improve students’ teamwork and develop leadership skills.
Being creative helps students to become better problem solvers in all areas of their life and work. Instead of coming from a linear, logical approach, creativity helps you see things differently and better deal with uncertainty.
Volunteering can provide a healthy boost to students’ self-confidence, self-esteem, and life satisfaction. Doing good for others and the community provides a natural sense of accomplishment and volunteering contributes to a sense of pride in one's identity.
Academic activities encourage students to develop their intellectual curiosity, expand their depth of knowledge in a particular area and develop the key skills needed for successful independent study.
A range of activities focussed on helping students to focus on self-awareness, providing them with a healthy means of defining their identities in positive and proactive ways.
Our Interest activities provide students with an opportunity to try new and exciting things they might not have had the opportunity to experience before. It also allows our teachers to share their passions with the students.
The activities on offer enable our students to broaden their horizons and develop a skill set suited to the modern world. We greatly appreciate it when parents encourage their children to get involved and attend as many clubs and societies throughout the week as possible. Clubs run before school, at lunchtime and after school and therefore are a great way to positively extend the school day.

Confidence & Character We develop resilience, kindness and self-belief alongside academic knowledge, preparing young people for life — not just exams.
Ambition for All We challenge every pupil to aim high, whether their strengths lie in academics, creativity, sport or leadership.
A True Community Visitors often comment on the warmth of our school. Relationships here matter, and pupils feel they belong.
PASTORAL CARE PROMISE
Children thrive when they feel happy, secure and valued. Pastoral care is not an add-on at St Edward’s — it is at the heart of everything we do.
Every pupil is known. Every pupil is supported. Every pupil matters.
St Edward’s has transformed our child’s confidence. The teachers genuinely care, and the difference in both happiness and progress has been remarkable.

Training & Fixtures
We run an extensive training and fixtures programme each term and are committed to each team having at least one fixture per week either during the week or on Saturdays. Along with the major games of Hockey, Rugby, Netball, Football and Cricket, we also provide competitive opportunities in Swimming, Athletics and Tennis.
Regional & National Achievements
St Edward’s teams have enjoyed both Regional and National success within the ISA Sport network and also perform successfully at District and County level. The School also boasts a large number of individual students who have achieved representative honours at District, County, Regional and National level in a wide variety of sports.
Sports Clubs
St Edward’s provides an extensive club timetable throughout the year during lunchtimes and after school. All students are encouraged to attend these sessions to develop their skills and gameplay but to also make firm social bonds. Our sport provision is both competitive and a recreational option.
STEPS
The St Edward’s Excellence Programme and Scholars (STEPS) is an integral part of our commitment to support and develop our most talented sporting students. The programme is designed to stretch and challenge our elite performers both in their physical performance and in their tactical play.
The Physical Education Department also offers academic courses at both GCSE and A Level with a number of St Edward’s students continuing to study a variety of Sports Science courses at university.

A full programme of Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) is delivered to students throughout their Senior School journey, primarily within PSHE lessons. When students move into Upper School they then engage with a variety of resources to: enhance their awareness of the different post-16 pathways available, understand the impact that particular choices may make upon their futures, and recognise how their skills and abilities may suit specific job roles.
All students also have access to Unifrog, an online platform that enables access to a broad range of career choices, as well as information on universities and different levels of apprenticeships where they can research their career ideas further.
Sixth Form Students
The Careers Lead is regularly available for Sixth Form students to discuss their thoughts and choices regarding what they want to do beyond Sixth Form. There is access to a broad range of information on these different pathways, as well as ICT packages to explore the opportunities available. Students are able to access this information throughout the school day during study periods, break, lunch and after school.
CEIAG provision is also delivered via PSHE lessons and then followed up by the Careers Lead and the UCAS Co-ordinator during assemblies and tutor periods.
University Applications
All Sixth Form students will register with UCAS (University and Colleges Admissions Service) at the end of the Summer Term in Lower Sixth There is a well-structured process for supporting students with university applications (both through UCAS and overseas) and emphasis is placed upon students to take control of their futures early on by being proactive and responsible for their own pathways. The UCAS coordinator is regularly available to advise on university applications. Our recent leaver destinations show the wide range of institutions and courses our students progress on to.

Fast Facts
St Edward's at a glance:
Tucked away behind its unassuming gates, St Edward’s sits on 20 acres of beautiful school grounds, with an additional 40 acres of sports fields just along London Road — the perfect environment for pupils to learn, play, and grow.
Our historic site, Charlton Park, was once a hunting lodge belonging to Edward the Confessor (1003–1066), giving our school a unique sense of heritage and charm.
St Edward’s has a tradition of nurturing exceptional talent. Our alumni include multi-award-winning actor Josh O’Connor, celebrated for his portrayal of Prince Charles in Netflix’s The Crown, and soon to be starring in the third Knives Out movie, alongside many others who have gone on to excel in all walks of life.
In January 2022, St Edward’s joined Alpha Schools, one of the UK’s leading independent school groups, opening the door to unprecedented opportunities for long-term stability, growth, innovation, and excellence.
Our pursuit of excellence has been widely recognised: in 2024–25 we were shortlisted for the Independent School of the Year at the Education Today School and Supplier Awards for outstanding academic outcomes, pastoral support and community impact.
Together, these strengths make St Edward’s a place where pupils are supported to flourish academically, socially and personally — ready for the opportunities ahead.
